open_obligations: Check whether samples from one model have correlated errors that violate Choi et al.'s independence assumption.
Note that Goel et al.'s similarity is across different models, not repeated samples.
Check Choi et al.'s condition that the correct answer is the most probable option.
in.other_title: Correlated failures risk: deferring to AI oversight as model blind spots converge
in.rationale: Choi, Zhu and Li prove majority voting succeeds with probability approaching 1 as N grows, assuming homogeneous independent agents whose top belief is on the correct answer. Goel et al. report more capable models make more similar mistakes and argue this weakens LM juries through compromised independence; Goel et al. measure similarity across models from different developers, while Choi et al.'s agents are samples from one model, so the challenge is to the independence assumption in practice.
in.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether adding more LLM voters reliably drives majority-vote accuracy toward 1

open_obligations: Note that Liang et al.'s judge-managed two-debater MAD differs from N-agent voting.
Check the independence assumption against real LLM samples.
Check whether more agents help when the correct answer is not the modal one.
out.other_title: Future work: more agents, board games, AI feedback for alignment via debate
out.rationale: Liang et al. list scheduling more agents as future work. Choi, Zhu and Li prove that majority voting over N homogeneous independent agents picks the correct answer with probability at least 1 - exp(-N (Delta/sqrt(K) - 1/sqrt(N))^2) when N > K/Delta^2, and find debate adds little beyond voting; Liang et al.'s MAD has two adversarial debaters and a judge, not N voters.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: how adding more agents affects multi-agent decisions, for majority voting over independent LLM agents

text: Assuming homogeneous independent agents whose initial belief is largest on the correct answer, with margin Delta between the top two Dirichlet means and K options, the authors prove that if N > K/Delta^2 then majority voting selects the correct answer with probability at least 1 - exp(-N (Delta/sqrt(K) - 1/sqrt(N))^2). They remark that this holds even when the correct answer's probability is well below one half, provided it is the most probable option.
title: Majority voting success probability approaches 1 as the number of agents grows
